figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Tetronate natural products. (A) Representative tetronate structures. The green moiety is tetronate, while the blue and red parts are formed
through catalysis by two distinct classes of Diels−Alder enzymes or their homologous proteins, respectively. (B) The biosynthetic gene clusters for
abyssomicin (aby), chlorothricin (chl), tetronasin (tsn) and lucensimycin A (luc). The homologous enzymes responsible for decalin and spirotetronate
biosynthesis are color-coded. To highlight the homology across these gene clusters, the large PKS genes are depicted in a scaled-down manner. (C)
Proposed biosynthetic pathway for 1.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Biosynthesis of 1 verified by in vivo and in vitro experiments. (A) HPLC analysis of metabolic extracts from the wild-type and mutant strains.
B) HPLC analysis of biochemical reactions catalyzed by different reconstituted enzyme sets. (C) HPLC analysis of the LucK-catalyzed reaction in vitro.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Crystal structures of LucK. (A) The overall structure of the dimer architecture of LucK. The unresolved N-terminal loop region is highlighted
with dashed lines. (B) Top view of the cavity in the β-barrel of LucK. (C) Surface charge potential representation (contoured at ± 63 kcal/mol; blue/
red) shows the acidic cavity. (D) Surface representation shows the hydrophobic or polar residues (gray and violet). (E) Key polar residues around the
substrate 7 at the bottom of β-barrel. (F) Key residues around the tetronate. (G) Relative enzyme activities of LucK and its site-specific mutants. Error
bars indicate the standard deviation of three independent replicates. (H) Proposed catalytic mechanism of LucK.
